title: Round 26 Illinois-Indiana state-frame USGS GNIS source register
scope: All-GNIS starter registers for Illinois and Indiana. Every seeded row reproduces one USGS GNIS record screened by exact official name, returned type/state/county, permanent FEATURE_ID, and returned GNIS primary point, and cross-checked on two independent USGS surfaces (USGS GNIS Geocoder; staged-products DomesticNames text via tools/gnis_extract.py; cumulative candidate extract resources/city-subsurface/gnis-candidates-batch7.json with per-state ZIP SHA-256 values). Charles Mound and Hoosier Hill additionally carry Domestic Names per-ID identity checks.

usgsGeocoder.use: Fuzzy candidate discovery only. A candidate was accepted only when Name, Type, State, County, GnisId, Latitude, and Longitude all matched the intended feature. Counties, canals, pools, flowages, navigation pools, old channels, historical places, and same-name records of another class or county were rejected explicitly where relevant.

gnisDomesticNames.use: Second-surface cross-check of every seeded FEATURE_ID and per-ID identity checks for Charles Mound (423586) and Hoosier Hill (1851956), extracted in a GitHub Actions runner by tools/gnis_extract.py. The current text layout carries no elevation columns, so the two high-point elevations cite USGS-published state-highpoint values. The candidate extract file is cumulative across batches 7-9; this register is the frozen batch-9 evidence.

selectionRules: VERIFIED=1 is claimed only for an exact official name, compatible GNIS feature class/type, intended state and returned primary county, permanent FEATURE_ID, and an official point returned by a cited USGS service, reproduced identically on the second USGS surface.

Grouped Geocoder Types map explicitly to stored row classes: Cities & Populated Places to Populated Place, Lakes & Reservoirs to Lake for the accepted named lakes, Streams & Canals to Stream for the accepted river records, and Summit to Summit.
A stored GNIS primary point is never described as a municipal boundary, street-address geocode, generic centroid, shoreline polygon, summit outline, or river centerline.

If exact-name candidates remain indistinguishable, or the state-filtered screen returns no intended feature record, the feature is omitted from that state gazetteer and may appear only as a generalized context corridor.
Statewide frames use explicitly synthetic relief gaussians and generalized corridors; no bundled DEM or surveyed boundary is implied.

knownLimitations: Illinois and Indiana are starter registers, not statewide GNIS extracts. Each contains 12 deliberately selected identity-safe rows.

The USGS Geocoder is a suggestion service; exact-match screening by name/type/state/county/FEATURE_ID is part of the evidence. Every seeded row was reproduced on the second USGS surface (staged-products DomesticNames text) at the same primary point.

The current DomesticNames text layout carries no elevation columns, so Charles Mound (1,235 feet) and Hoosier Hill (1,257 feet) elevations cite USGS-published state-highpoint values; GNIS identity for both rests on the per-ID class/county/point reproduction.
GNIS point data do not supply the displayed terrain or corridors. Both frames use explicitly synthetic relief gaussians and generalized context lines.
State frames are rectangles, not state-boundary clipping masks. Both rectangles include small areas outside their state outlines; no boundary geometry is claimed.
